title: Infra GPU fleet capacity + networking + IaC + CI/CD runbook (proactive maintenance)
author: Aisha Rahman
body:
Overview

This runbook documents proactive maintenance, capacity planning, and operational playbooks for the Redwood Inference GPU fleet, associated cloud accounts and networking, and the Terraform/CI-CD modules used to manage the fleet. The intended audience is infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners responsible for capacity, deployments, and incident handling.

Goals

- Maintain sufficient GPU capacity to meet production SLOs while minimizing idle-costs.
- Keep Terraform/IaC modules and CI/CD pipelines deterministic and auditable.
- Minimize impact of planned maintenance and cloud account/networking changes.
- Provide clear, step-by-step operational procedures for scale, patch, and rollback.

Scope

Applies to: Redwood-hosted Dedicated and Private deployment fleet, cloud accounts in AWS (primary), GCP (secondary), and on-prem nodes managed via the onprem packaging pipelines. Covers: GPU instance profiles, autoscaling policies, Terraform module usage, CI/CD build flows, networking requirements, runbook procedures, and monitoring/alerting thresholds.

Owner & Contacts

- Primary owner: Infra Engineering (capacity subgroup)
- Runbook author: Aisha Rahman (Infra Eng)
- Pager: infra-oncall@redwood.example.com
- Escalation: Senior Infra Eng (L2) -> SRE Manager (L3) -> Head of Platform (L4)

SLOs & Capacity Targets

- Target sustained GPU utilization (production pools): 65% average over 1 week.
- Spike headroom: ability to absorb 2x traffic for up to 10 minutes without queueing.
- Queue time SLO for inference requests routed to Dedicated pools: p95 < 50ms queue time, p99 < 200ms.
- Fleet replenishment SLA: provision new capacity in a region within 30 minutes for automated scale, or 90 minutes for manual provisioning.

Fleet topology and node types

- GPU profiles in use (example):
  - gpu.h100-80g-large (primary high-performance for latency-sensitive models)
  - gpu.a100-40g-medium (cost-performance mix for batch/throughput workloads)
  - gpu.t4-16g-small (embedding and low-cost inference)

- Node role tags: workload=generation|embeddings|batch, environment=prod|staging|dev, region=us-east-1|eu-west-1|ap-southeast-1

Terraform / IaC modules (structure & conventions)

Summary:
- Terraform is the canonical source for fleet infrastructure (instances, autoscaling groups, ASG policies, load-balancers, network interfaces, IAM roles). State is stored in a remote backend (S3 + DynamoDB for AWS) per-account, per-region.

Key modules (examples):
- modules/gpu-instance: defines instance types, AMI lookup, disk layout, instance metadata and tags.
- modules/gpu-asg: autoscaling group with mixed instances, lifecycle hooks for graceful termination, and Spot fallback policy.
- modules/networking: VPC, subnets, route-tables, security-groups, NATs, and peering for private deployments.
- modules/iam: IAM roles/policies scoped for node bootstrap, kubelet, metrics push, and secrets access.

Conventions:
1. Module outputs use stable names: instance_profile_arn, asg_name, lb_dns.
2. Use workspace naming: <account>-<region>-<env>.
3. Keep state isolation: production workspaces are write-protected and require PR and at least two approvers.

CI/CD & Build pipelines

- Pipelines exist in the central infra repo and are run in the platform CI system. Typical stages:
  1) terraform fmt/checks and module unit tests
  2) plan with a deterministic TF_VAR set and remote workspace selection
  3) integration run in a non-prod workspace (smoke apply for ephemeral resources)
  4) PR review, security/lgtm checks, manual approval for prod
  5) apply to prod with drift detection agent post-apply

- Artifact management: AMI/image builds are done via Packer pipelines. Images are versioned with semantic tags (e.g. redwood-gpu-node-2026.02.10). CI will refuse to deploy AMIs not in the approved artifact registry for prod.

Network & Cloud Accounts (requirements)

Minimal networking checklist for a new region/account:
- VPC with at least 3 availability zones with private subnets and NATs.
- CIDR allocation plan documented and approved (avoid overlapping with customer VPCs for Private deployments).
- Dedicated Transit Gateway or VPC Peering configuration for cross-account management traffic.
- Security groups: allow control-plane ports (SSH from bastion, node metrics outbound to monitoring, kubelet if applicable).
- Flow logs: enabled for VPC and subnets; logs shipped to centralized logging account.

Table: required IAM scopes for infra automation

| Role | Minimum policies | Notes |
|------|------------------|-------|
| infra-deploy-bot | EC2:Create/Terminate, IAM:PassRole, S3:GetObject, DynamoDB:Lock | Used by CI to apply TF state |
| image-builder | EC2:CreateImage, SSM:SendCommand | Packer image builds |
| monitoring-push | CloudWatch:PutMetricData, Logs:PutLogEvents | Node metrics and logs |

Runbook: common operational procedures

1) Detecting capacity pressure (automated triggers)
   - Alerts: CPU/GPU utilization > 85% average for 10m across prod-pool -> page infra-oncall.
   - Metric anomalies: sustained increase in request rate beyond rolling baseline (20% uplift over 15m).

2) Immediate mitigation (first 15 minutes)
   1. Confirm alert and scope via dashboards (per-region GPU usage, per-pool queue depth).
   2. If autoscaling policies are enabled and ASG has capacity, allow automated scale for up to 10 minutes.
   3. If ASG failed to scale (Spot reclaim, quota), perform manual scale:
      - Terraform hack (temporary): increase desired_capacity on asg via console or tf apply to the asg workspace.
      - Alternative: trigger Image-based ephemeral instances via the runbook script (scripts/ephemeral-scale.sh) to add nodes to the LB for 30-90 mins.
   4. Re-route low-priority traffic to cheaper pools (tag: workload=batch) by updating routing policy in the smart router (console).

3) Post-incident remediation (30m-6h)
   - Audit why autoscale failed: check Spot interruptions, IAM quota errors, cloud provider limits.
   - If quota limits are hit, open cloud support case and attach autoscale logs and TF plan.
   - Schedule capacity purchase (reserve instances or commit Dedicated capacity) if frequent spikes persist.

4) Planned maintenance / image rotation procedure (standard maintenance window)
   Preconditions:
   - Notify platform slack channel and send calendar invite to oncall 72 hours prior.
   - Confirm health of all regions with green SLOs for 48 hours.

   Steps:
   1. Create new AMI via Packer pipeline with security and runtime updates.
   2. Create a blue ASG with the new AMI in staging workspace. Run e2e smoke tests (container start, hello inference).
   3. Canary rollout: Add 2 nodes to prod pool and route 1% traffic for 30 minutes. Monitor error rates and latency.
   4. If stable, increase to 20% traffic for 60 minutes then full shift. If regressions appear, revert traffic and terminate canary ASG.
   5. Cleanup old images and update AMI registry entry.

Rollback checklist

- If new AMI causes increased latency or errors: revert routing to previous ASG via LB, then rollback terraform change to previous AMI id and run apply in prod workspace.
- If Terraform provider error prevents apply: revert by restoring previous state snapshot and coordinate with state-owner.

Monitoring & Alerts (recommended thresholds)

- GPU utilization: p95 < 95% (alert), p50 target ~65%
- Queue depth: alert when queue depth > 200 requests for >5 minutes
- Node health: alert on >10% nodes reporting disk pressure or OOM events in a single pool
- TF drift: alert on resource drift detected by drift-detector job (daily)

Automation & tooling tips

- Use the infra CLI wrapper: infra tf plan <workspace> --auto-approve=false to generate reproducible plans with a link to the run ID.
- Preflight checks: infra preflight <region> validates quotas, AMI availability, and subnet attachment before a prod apply.
- Canary automation: the canary-runner job will automatically scale a canary ASG and route traffic when given a canary manifest file.

Troubleshooting checklist (quick)

- No capacity available for scale:
  - Check cloud quotas and spot capacity metrics.
  - Verify billing/limits not paused by finance.
  - Check for stuck lifecycle hooks or unattached instances in ASG.

- Autoscaling failed to apply TF change:
  - Inspect TF plan for resource replacements that require manual intervention.
  - Check remote state lock (DynamoDB) — force-unlock only after coordination.

- Networking errors between control plane and nodes:
  - Validate security-group rules and route tables. Check VPC flow logs for rejected traffic.
  - Confirm Transit Gateway attachments and peering status.

Maintenance windows and blackout policy

- Planned maintenance allowed in the following windows by default (region local times):
  - Weekdays: 02:00-05:00 (low traffic) and Weekends: 03:00-07:00.
- Emergency maintenance may be scheduled outside windows with explicit oncall approval.
- Blackout windows for critical customers (private deployments) must be observed; coordinate with customer-success and account teams.

Postmortem & continuous improvement

- For any incident where SLO breach > 1 hour or repeated auto-scale failures occur, open a postmortem in the oncall-and-incident-response space and assign action items.
- Quarterly capacity review: capacity owners must publish a short report with utilization trends, forecast, and suggested investments (reserved capacity or instance family changes).

Appendices

- Useful commands:
  - infra tf plan --workspace=prod-us-east-1 --var-file=prod.tfvars
  - infra preflight us-east-1
  - scripts/ephemeral-scale.sh --count 4 --ami redwood-gpu-node-2026.02.10

- Related pages and runbooks:
  - /confluence/eng-infra/terraform-and-iac/infra-iac-and-gpu-fleet-guide-2026.json
  - /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026.json
